title: US Clean Power Rises With Data Centers: Three Things to Know | BloombergNEF
gist: BNEF sees US data-center capacity rising from 47GW (2025) to 194GW (2035), driving over 1TW of solar, wind and storage additions in 2026-2036 and record builds of 89GW/93GW in 2026/2027 backed by a 250GW+ safe-harbored tax-credit pipeline. Storage (+34% to 383GW) and wind are revised up while tariffs cut utility solar, PFE rules chill bank financing, and on-site gas (165GW announced) currently wins on cost and speed for data-center load.

insights.claim: BloombergNEF expects the US to add more than 1 terawatt of solar, wind and energy storage capacity from 2026 to 2036, over twice the cumulative installed capacity at end-2025, even as federal tax credits phase out.
insights.speaker: dsimon110
insights.so_what: Decade-long demand runway for US renewables and storage supply chains despite subsidy phase-out.
insights.quote: more than 1-terawatt of solar, wind and energy storage capacity from 2026 to 2036
insights.locator: 1. Data-center demand lifts US clean power outlook

insights.claim: Under BloombergNEF's base case, total installed US data-center capacity rises roughly fourfold from 47GW in 2025 to 194GW in 2035.
insights.speaker: dsimon110
insights.so_what: Scale of AI/data-center load growth is the core demand signal for power generation, grid and equipment investors.
insights.quote: The total installed data-center capacity in the US reaches 194 gigawatts in 2035 from 47GW in 2025
insights.locator: BNEF expects the US to add

insights.claim: Data-center electricity demand is the key growth lever for US clean power beyond the pipeline of projects already supported by tax credits.
insights.speaker: dsimon110
insights.so_what: Post-2030 renewables growth hinges on hyperscaler procurement rather than subsidies.
insights.quote: Data center demand remains the key growth lever for clean power beyond the tax-credit-supported pipeline.
insights.locator: Data center demand remains the key

insights.claim: Higher carbon prices, state-level procurement, decarbonization targets and corporate clean energy buyers support US clean power deployment, while regulatory uncertainty and higher financing and equipment costs temper growth.
insights.speaker: dsimon110
insights.so_what: Identifies the levers to monitor for upside/downside to the US renewables build forecast.

themes.theme: Storage and wind up, utility solar down

insights.claim: BloombergNEF expects 383GW of US energy storage additions from 2026 to 2036, up 34% from its May 2026 outlook.
insights.speaker: dsimon110
insights.so_what: Storage is the biggest upward revision, favoring battery makers, integrators and storage developers.
insights.quote: BNEF expects 383 gigawatts of energy storage additions from 2026 to 2036, up 34%
insights.locator: The stronger clean-power outlook is uneven

insights.claim: BloombergNEF raised its 2026-2036 US onshore wind forecast by 15% to 100GW.
insights.speaker: dsimon110
insights.so_what: Onshore wind outlook improving, a modest positive for turbine OEMs and wind developers.
insights.quote: the onshore wind forecast has risen 15%, to 100GW
insights.locator: The stronger clean-power outlook is uneven

insights.claim: BloombergNEF cut expected 2026-2036 US utility-scale solar additions by 7.5% to 430GW because new solar-specific import tariffs weaken project economics.
insights.speaker: dsimon110
insights.so_what: Tariffs are directly eroding the US utility solar opportunity, a headwind for solar developers and module suppliers.
insights.quote: expected utility-scale solar additions have fallen 7.5%, to 430GW, as new solar-specific import tariffs weaken project economics
insights.locator: The stronger clean-power outlook is uneven

themes.theme: Safe-harbored pipeline and PFE financing risk

insights.claim: BloombergNEF forecasts US solar, wind and storage additions of 89GW in 2026 and 93GW in 2027, two consecutive record years of build.
insights.speaker: dsimon110
insights.so_what: Near-term record installations support 2026-2027 revenue visibility for clean-energy equipment and EPC firms.
insights.quote: BNEF forecasts 89GW of solar, wind and energy storage capacity additions in 2026, and then 93GW in 2027

insights.claim: The near-term US build record is underpinned by wind and solar projects that began construction by the July 4, 2026 deadline, preserving eligibility for the 48E/45Y federal tax credits.
insights.speaker: dsimon110
insights.so_what: Policy pull-forward front-loads deployment, implying a potential air pocket once the safe-harbored pipeline is exhausted.

insights.claim: Under BloombergNEF's optimistic safe-harbor scenario, the US has more than 250GW of tax-credit-eligible solar and wind capacity in the pipeline, most of which is expected to come online by end-2030.
insights.speaker: dsimon110
insights.so_what: A quantified, subsidy-protected backlog that de-risks build volumes through 2030.
insights.quote: the US has more than 250GW of tax-credit-eligible solar and wind capacity in the pipeline

insights.claim: Banks are hesitant to fund US renewable projects exposed to not-yet-finalized prohibited foreign entity (PFE) rules, which restrict tax-credit projects from using equipment tied to designated countries such as China.
insights.speaker: dsimon110
insights.so_what: Final PFE guidance is a key catalyst; its release could unlock stalled project financing and shift sourcing away from Chinese supply.
insights.quote: Banks are hesitant to fund projects exposed to yet-to-be-finalized PFE rules.

insights.claim: Despite PFE uncertainty, the stock of projects retaining legacy tax credits or exempt from PFE rules is large enough for US clean power deployment to continue.
insights.speaker: dsimon110
insights.so_what: Suggests PFE fears may be overdone for near-term deployment volumes.
insights.locator: Nevertheless, the stock of projects retaining

insights.claim: Tariffs on solar equipment and restrictions on foreign-made inverters and other bulk-power system equipment are raising costs for solar, storage and grid infrastructure, though tax-credit projects can still absorb the higher costs.
insights.speaker: dsimon110
insights.so_what: Protectionism benefits domestic equipment makers while squeezing developer margins, especially for projects without tax credits.
insights.quote: Projects wielding tax credits can still absorb higher costs, but these measures add risks to the deployment outlook.
insights.locator: Protectionist measures are also increasing pressure

themes.theme: On-site gas competes for data-center load

insights.claim: On-site natural gas generation could meet a sizable share of rising US data-center electricity demand, potentially reducing the near-term role of renewables.
insights.speaker: dsimon110
insights.so_what: Behind-the-meter gas is a direct competitor to renewables PPAs and a tailwind for gas turbine makers and gas producers.
insights.quote: On-site natural gas generation could meet a sizable share of rising US data-center electricity demand
insights.locator: 3. Onsite gas power offers a competitive option

insights.claim: Gas currently beats alternatives on both speed and cost for data centers' very high availability needs, because renewables-plus-storage must be heavily oversized and nuclear/SMR clean firm power has much longer development timelines.
insights.speaker: dsimon110
insights.so_what: Time-to-power is the decisive metric for data-center power; gas wins now, while SMRs remain a longer-dated bet.
insights.quote: Renewables paired with storage need to be significantly oversized and therefore require higher spending to deliver ongoing reliable power
insights.locator: Gas currently has advantages in both

insights.claim: BloombergNEF modeling of a 1GW IT-capacity data center in PJM, sized for 99.999% reliability from fully behind-the-meter resources with RGGI carbon costs applied, finds gas wins on all-in cost.
insights.speaker: dsimon110
insights.so_what: Even with carbon costs, gas is the cost-leading off-grid option in PJM, the key US data-center market.
insights.locator: Gas Wins on Cost to Meet

insights.claim: BloombergNEF tracks 165GW of announced on-site gas generation projects at US data centers, but the pipeline is highly uncertain, with many projects lacking a proposed in-service date or identified equipment suppliers.
insights.speaker: dsimon110
insights.so_what: Headline on-site gas pipeline is likely inflated; investors should discount announcements without turbine supply secured.
insights.quote: many projects missing a proposed in-service date and identified equipment suppliers

insights.claim: Tighter emissions rules, restrictions on new gas permitting or a higher carbon price could erode the economics of gas-fired generation and shift more data-center demand toward clean power.
insights.speaker: dsimon110
insights.so_what: Policy risk to the gas-for-data-centers trade; a regulatory shift would favor renewables and storage.
insights.locator: The gas advantage is also not guaranteed.

insights.claim: Many on-site gas plants at data centers will need batteries for redundancy, efficiency and protection against fluctuating AI power loads, creating a complementary storage market.
insights.speaker: dsimon110
insights.so_what: Second-order demand for battery storage even in gas-powered data centers, benefiting BESS suppliers either way.
insights.quote: many on-site gas plants at data centers will need to have batteries installed to provide redundancy and boost efficiency
